newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares up on fears of missing rally boat.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares up on fears of missing rally boat.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Monday, as investors snapped up paper out of fear of missing the boat in January, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 0.98 percent on $7.83 million in volume.

"Everything firmed today," said Alexander Fonarkov, a trader from Regent European Securities. "Some people are afraid they will not have time to buy enough shares after the post-New Year rally starts. Everyone wants to sit on paper."
Traders said they saw some Western demand despite the approaching Christmas holidays.
Vladislav Leonchuk, a trader from ING Bank, said the rise was also due to brokers' closing of short positions ahead of the end of the year.
Fonarkov said investors focused on LUKoil and UES.
LUKoil rose to $10.64 from $10.46 at Friday's close and UES was $0.0846 after $0.0849.
Leonchuk said some second-tier shares fell due to an increasing inflow of shares from the regions.
Novosibirsknenergo, a second-tier, fell to $2.40 from $2.50 at December 15 close, when it was last traded.
Novosibirskaya Telefonnaya Set was the gain leader of the day, with prices rising to $12.00 from $11.70.
Traders forecast the market would see low volume trade until the end of the year.
Mosenergo was $0.980 after $0.972, Irkutskenergo slipped to $0.124 from $0.127, Rostelekom rose to $2.32 from $2.28 and Norilsk Nickel was unchanged at $5.15.
